item.text:
**4B.2 Research Note**

Overall judgment: **No**. The 2024 record does not show Sharif refraining from manipulating the field to entrench himself. The strongest evidence is negative: election-day communication shutdowns, party-symbol / election-rule disadvantages for opponents, judicial restructuring, and repeated coercive responses to dissent. The best pro-side evidence is procedural only: he came in through a hung parliament and a formal parliamentary vote, which shows contestation still existed, but not a clear commitment to fair competition.

- [Shehbaz Sharif to be coalition candidate for next Pakistan PM -spokeswoman](https://theprint.in/world/shehbaz-sharif-to-be-coalition-candidate-for-next-pakistan-pm-spokeswoman/1965379/) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-14. Claim: After a hung parliament, Sharif’s route back to office depended on coalition bargaining, which is the main pro-contestability fact in the record; it shows power was still negotiated rather than automatically inherited. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 4B.1.

- [Shehbaz Sharif elected Pakistan’s prime minister for second term](https://theprint.in/india/shehbaz-sharif-elected-pakistans-prime-minister-for-second-term/1986782/) - **Reuters**, 2024-03-03. Claim: Parliament formally elected Sharif, so the transfer of power remained procedurally contestable; however, the result was immediately disputed by opponents as rigged, so this is only weak positive evidence. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 4B.1.

- [Pakistan’s Imran Khan’s party loses cricket bat electoral symbol](https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-imran-khans-party-loses-cricket-bat-electoral-symbol/1923216/) - **Reuters**, 2024-01-14. Claim: Pakistan’s Supreme Court upheld the Election Commission’s removal of PTI’s bat symbol on technical intra-party-election grounds, which was a legally framed but materially disadvantageous electoral-rule change for Sharif’s main opponent. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 4B.1.

- [US, UK and EU urge probe into Pakistan election, express concerns](https://www.theprint.in/world/us-uk-eu-urge-probe-into-pakistan-election-express-concerns/1961577/) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-10. Claim: Major external partners publicly cited concerns about irregularities, interference, and fraud and urged a probe, which is strong counterevidence that the election environment was clean or fully contestable. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 4B.1.

- [US concerned about reports of intimidation, voter suppression in Pakistan election, White House says](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/us-concerned-about-reports-of-intimidation-voter-suppression-in-pakistan-election-white-house-says-3305341) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-15. Claim: The White House explicitly raised intimidation and voter-suppression concerns, reinforcing that the electoral contest was not being treated as free and fair. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 4B.1.

- [Pakistan: Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-02-08. Claim: Telecommunications and mobile internet were shut down on election day, which Amnesty called a blunt attack on expression and assembly; this is direct evidence of a coercive election environment, though it was carried out by the caretaker setup rather than Sharif’s cabinet. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9, 4B.1.

- [Pakistan: The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-09-09. Claim: The government rushed through a new protest law that Amnesty said criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded authority to ban or restrict gatherings, showing entrenchment through legal restriction rather than neutral rule-setting. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9.

- [Pakistan Government Intensifies Crackdown on Political Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024-10-09. Claim: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against PTI protesters, including peaceful demonstrators, which is strong evidence of using security forces and public controls to suppress opponents. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9.

- [Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) - **The Guardian**, 2024-10-21. Claim: The 26th Amendment changed senior-judge appointment rules in a way critics said weakened judicial independence, and it passed amid allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs; this is direct evidence against refraining from court manipulation. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 3B.4.

- [Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-11-27. Claim: Amnesty described deaths, mass detentions, shutdowns, and a pattern of intolerance for peaceful protest during the Islamabad crackdown, which is the clearest year-end evidence that the government was not simply leaving political competition open. **Question IDs:** 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9.

Search gap: I found **no strong 2024 source showing Sharif affirmatively committed to keeping elections fully free, fair, and meaningfully contestable** or to insulating courts/media/election administration from political advantage. The positive evidence is procedural and limited; the balance of the record points the other way.
